Lead origin: inbound self-serve. Company builds developer tools that add chat + code assistant to client dashboards. Wants a hosted API path (fast time-to-value) but expects to scale to Dedicated within 12-18 months.

Call notes / paraphrases: ‘We love Redwood docs but need direct examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex adapters. Also want a Vercel Next.js (Edge) sample that uses the Vercel AI SDK with Redwood hosted keys.’ CTO: ‘Latency target ~300-500ms for assistant flows, cost sensitive since freemium userbase.’

Integration details observed:
- Tried LangChain (python) Agent with SimpleSequentialChain + Redwood completion backend; developer saw 401 on the first run (forgot to set REDWOOD_API_KEY in env) then intermittent 429 when running larger simulation.
- Experimented with LlamaIndex (now called "LlamaIndex") doc loader for S3 -> built index, but embeddings call returned higher latency (1.2s) vs expected ~400ms. Wants embedding batching examples.
- Frontend team wants an example repo: Next.js + Vercel AI SDK -> using Redwood hosted API key via serverless edge function. Concern: how to safely store/restrict keys for client-side calls.

Requested deliverables from our side:
- Short LangChain Python adapter quickstart (Agent + tool example) that sets up retries and backoff for 429, example for session/KV cache reuse.
- LlamaIndex notebook showing document ingestion -> batched embeddings -> index storage, with recommended model/quantization profiles for cost reduction.
- Vercel AI SDK sample (Next.js 14) showing server-side route that proxies to Redwood hosted_api, with example env var setup and per-route rate limiting suggestions.
- Clarify hosted API token scopes, rate-limit tiers, and guidance on routing/fallback (e.g., fallback to smaller model during bursts).
